observed_behavior: Rollback deletes a byte-identical independently replaced first pair entry when publication of the second entry collides.
expected_behavior: Pair publication preserves every independent entry and rolls back only a first target whose file identity and bytes still prove ownership by the current writer.
impact: Create-only preliminary review or Outcome history can lose an independently owned entry, leaving an incomplete audit chain.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: Both collision codes are returned while the byte-identical independently replaced first entry and the second competitor remain present.
steps: Publish the first entry of an initially absent two-file pair.
Remove that directory entry and independently recreate it with byte-identical content.
Create a competitor at the second target immediately before its atomic publication and inspect rollback state.
reproduction.sample: Windows and Linux each produced only the expected regression failures: two subtest failures report that rollback deleted the independent first entry; both fresh-review probes reported first_exists_after_rollback=false.

root_cause.summary: _rollback_pair_publication equates payload byte equality with writer ownership, so it deletes a byte-identical independent replacement.

next_action: Implementation executor records publication file identity before commit, makes rollback conditional on both identity and bytes, then reruns Windows/Linux focused, full and fresh review.
